en: The Queen of Spells, Mahāmāyūrī: Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Mahāmāyūrī, the goddess who restores the dead to life and wards off malevolent beings.

I bow down to the Great-Souled Queen of Vidyās, Māyūrī; homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the Arhats, the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, future, and present; and to the entire Great Community of all Dharmas.

Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṅgha; homage to the seven perfectly awakened Buddhas together with their communities of disciples; homage to the Arhats in the world; homage to the Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, headed by Maitreya; homage to the Non-returners; homage to the Once-returners; homage to the Stream-enterers; homage to those who have gone rightly in the world; homage to those who have practiced rightly. Having paid homage to these, I shall employ this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās.

May this knowledge of mine be successful; may the hosts of spirits hear me! Whatever beings there are who move upon the earth, through the air, or in the water—gods, nāgas, asuras, maruts, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanās, kaṭapūtanās, skandas, unmādas, chāyās, apasmāras, ostārakas—may they hear me! May the hosts of spirits that consume vital energy, those that consume the fetus, those that consume blood, those that consume fat, those that consume flesh, and those that consume marrow hear me!

They feed on marrow, they feed on birth, they feed on life, they feed on strength, they feed on garlands, they feed on perfumes, they feed on incense, they feed on flowers, they feed on fruits, they feed on crops, they feed on oblations, they feed on worship, they feed on forced labor, they feed on urine, they feed on spittle, they feed on phlegm, they feed on snot, they feed on leftovers, they feed on vomit, they feed on impurities, they feed on drains; they possess evil minds, corrupt minds, and fierce minds, and they are the takers of the lives of others.

I shall proclaim this Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī; I shall offer incense, flowers, incense-sticks, lamps, and sacrificial oblations. May all those with evil minds, malicious minds, or fierce minds, who take the lives of others and steal vitality—may all such *grahas* hear me! And may those with gentle minds, loving minds, and virtuous minds, who have deep faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, hear me! It is as follows:

Kāli, Karāli, Kumbhāṇḍī, Śaṅkhinī, Kamalākṣī, Harītī, Harikeśī, Śrīmatī, Hari, Haripiṅgalā, Laṃbā, Pralaṃbā, Kālapāśā, Kālaśodarī, Yamadūtī, Yamarākṣasī, Bhūtagrasanī—accept me! I shall offer you fragrance, flowers, incense, and an oblation. Protect me, along with my attendants and retinue, and all sentient beings, from all fears and calamities. May he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns. May my mantra-words be successful! Svāhā!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great community of monks and a great community of bodhisattvas. Now at that time, a monk named Svāti was residing in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery.

There was a young man, very youthful, who had recently gone forth and recently received full ordination; having come but lately to this Dharma and Vinaya, while he was splitting wood for a sauna for the sake of the Saṅgha, a large black snake emerged from a certain rotten, hollow log and bit him on the big toe of his right foot. With his body exhausted, he fell to the ground and lay there, foaming at the mouth and rolling his eyes.

The venerable Ānanda saw a monk named Svāti who was afflicted, suffering, and severely ill; he had fallen to the ground, was vomiting foam, was rolling his eyes, and was drifting off to sleep. Having seen him, he went quickly and hurriedly to where the Blessed One was. Upon arriving, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable Ānanda addressed the Blessed One as follows.

"Lord, here in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, there dwells a monk named Svāti. He is new, young, and tender; he has recently gone forth, recently received full ordination, and has only recently come to this Dharma and Vinaya. While splitting wood for a sauna on behalf of the Saṅgha, a large black snake emerged from a hollow in a piece of putrid wood and bit him on the big toe of his right foot."
With his body exhausted, he falls to the ground, foaming at the mouth and rolling his eyes as he sleeps; O Blessed One, how should I conduct myself toward him?

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Ānanda: "Go, Ānanda, by the word of the Tathāgata, perform protection for the monk Svāti with this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Spells; provide him security, rescue, shelter, guardianship, peace, well-being, immunity from punishment, immunity from weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth."

From the seizure of gods, from the seizure of nāgas, from the seizure of asuras, from the seizure of maruts, from the seizure of garuḍas, from the seizure of gandharvas, from the seizure of kinnaras, from the seizure of mahoragas, from the seizure of yakṣas, from the seizure of rākṣasas, from the seizure of pretas, from the seizure of piśācas, from the seizure of bhūtas, from the seizure of kumbhāṇḍas, from the seizure of pūtanas, from the seizure of kaṭapūtanas, from the seizure of skandas, from the seizure of madness, from the seizure of shadows, from the seizure of epilepsy, and from the seizure of ostārakas.

[He is] free from *kṛtyā*, *karman*, *kākhorda*, *vetāḍa*, *kiraṇa*, *cicaka*, *preṣaka*, and [the effects of] bad food, vomit, bad shadows, evil glances, ill-drawn [images], transgressions, and being shaken off; [and he is free] from fever—whether quotidian, tertian, quartan, weekly, half-monthly, monthly, daily, momentary, constant, or irregular; and from fevers caused by spirits, human, or non-human, as well as those arising from wind, bile, phlegm, or all [three humors combined].

Remove headache, hemicrania, loss of appetite, eye disease, nose disease, mouth disease, throat disease, heart disease, constriction of the throat, earache, toothache, pain in the heart, pain in the back, pain in the sides, pain in the abdomen, pain in the genitals, pain in the womb, pain in the groin, pain in the bladder, pain in the thighs, pain in the calves, pain in the hands, pain in the feet, and remove all pain in the limbs and their members.
May there be well-being at night, well-being by day, and well-being when midday has arrived; may all the Buddhas grant me well-being throughout the entire day and night.

Namely: iḍi viḍi kiḍi hiḍi miḍi tiḍi āḍe ghāḍe durgāḍe hariṇi vaguḍi pāṃśu piśāci varṣaṇi ārohaṇi orohaṇi, ele mele tele tile, tili tile, mele mele, time time, dume dume, dudume dudume, iṭṭi miṭṭi viṣṭhande, capale vimale, hulu hulu hulu hulu, aśvamukhi, kāli kāli karāli mahākāli, prakīrṇakeśi, kulu kulu, vaphulu vaphulu kolu kolu hulu hulu, vahulu.

Vahulu, kolu kolu, hulu hulu, vahulu vahulu, vosā dumbā dodumbā domadumbā, golāyā velāyā parivelāyā, piśu piśu, hili hili hili hili hili hili hili hili hili hili, oṃ mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili. Oṃ tili tili tili tili tili tili tili tili tili tili. Oṃ culu culu culu culu culu culu culu culu culu culu.

Oṃ muhu muhu muhu muhu muhu muhu muhu muhu muhu. Oṃ mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu. Oṃ hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu. Oṃ hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu. Oṃ vā vā vā vā vā vā vā vā vā vā. Oṃ pā pā pā pā pā pā pā pā pā pā. Oṃ jāla jāla jāla jāla jāla jāla jāla jāla jāla.

Dama, Damani; Tapa, Tapani; Jvala, Jvalani; Paca, Pacani; Dundubhi, Garjani, Varṣaṇi, Sphoṭani; Tapani, Tāpani; Pacani, Pācani; Hariṇi, Hāriṇi; Kāliṇi, Kamali, Kaṃpani; Mardani; Maṇḍitike; Kṣemaṃkari; Makari, Śākari; Śarkari, Karkari, Savari, Śaṃkari; Jvalani, Jvalani; Dumadumbani, Sukusume; Golāyā, Velāyā, Parivelāyā—may the god rain everywhere! Ilikisi svāhā!
May I have loving-kindness toward the Dhṛtarāṣṭras and loving-kindness toward the Airāvaṇas.
My loving-kindness extends to the Virūpākṣas and to the Kṛṣṇagautamas;
my loving-kindness is with Maṇi, the king of nāgas, and with Vāsuki; and it is always with the Daṇḍapāda nāgas and the Pūrṇabhadras.
The two nāgas Nanda and Upananda, who are handsome, renowned, possessed of great supernatural power, and have experienced even the battle between the gods and asuras;
they maintain friendship with Anavatapta, Varuṇa, and Mandūka.
I have friendship with Takṣaka, Ananta, and likewise Vāsuki;
I have friendship with Aparājita and Chitrasena,
and always with Mahāmanasvin as well as Manasvin.
Kālaka and Apalāla, the venerable Śrāmaṇeraka, Dadhimukha and Maṇi, Pauṇḍarīka the lord of the quarters,
Karkoṭaka, Śaṅkhapāla, and both Kambala and Aśvatara.
And I always maintain loving-kindness toward these as well, toward the Naga kings:
Sāketa, Kumbhīra, and likewise Sūciloman.

I have always maintained friendship with Kāla, the lord of serpents, and with the seer Ṛṣika; likewise, I have friendship with Pūraṇa Karṇin and Śakaṭamukha, as well as with Koluka, Sunanda, and Vātsīputra.
I have friendship with Elapatra and Lambūka,
as well as with those non-human nāgas and likewise those who are superhuman;
and with the great nāga Mṛgila and the renowned Mucilinda.
Those nāgas who move upon the earth, as well as those who dwell in the water,
those who roam the atmosphere, and those who reside on Mount Meru— whether they have one head or two heads— I maintain constant loving-kindness toward them all.
May my loving-kindness be toward those without feet, and may my loving-kindness be toward those with two feet;
may my loving-kindness be toward those with four feet, and may my loving-kindness be toward those with many feet. May those without feet not harm me, and may those with two feet not harm me.
May four-footed creatures not harm me; may many-footed creatures not harm me.
I have loving-kindness toward all nāgas, those nāgas who dwell in the water; I have loving-kindness toward all beings, whoever they may be, who dwell upon the earth.
I have loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, including those beings here who are stationary;
may all sentient beings, all living creatures,
and all beings without exception, indeed be happy and free from all illness.
May all behold auspicious things; may no one encounter evil.
Having aroused a mind of loving-kindness, I perform the neutralization of poison, as well as protection, acceptance, and likewise preservation.
Homage be to the Buddha; homage be to awakening.
Homage be to the liberated one; homage be to liberation.
Homage be to the peaceful one, homage be to peace;
homage to the liberated one, homage to liberation. To those brahmins who have cast off all unwholesome states...
Homage to them! May they protect me.

From all fears, from all calamities, from all misfortunes and afflictions, from all fevers, from all diseases, from all planetary seizures, and from all poisons—may they grant protection to me and to all sentient beings; may we live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

Long ago, Ānanda, on the southern slope of Himavat, the king of mountains, there lived a peacock king named Suvarṇāvabhāsa. By means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās, he performed a rite of well-being at dawn and dwelt happily during the day; having performed a rite of well-being in the evening, he dwelt happily during the night. [He would say: "Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha! Homage to the Blessed Lady Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās! It is as follows:"

Hu hu hu hu hu hu, nāga le le le, dumba le le le, huya huya, vija vija, thusa thusa, guru guru, he cejini, agalu, elā melā, ili melā, tili melā, ili tili melā, ili mitte, tili mitte ili tili mitte, dumbe sudumbe, tosu tosu, golā velā capalā vimalā, iṭṭiri bhiṭṭiri riṭṭiri, homage to the Buddhas, to the Cilikis and Godohikas; homage to the Arhats! O Hāla, O Dāla, may the rain fall everywhere in the ten directions! Homage to the Buddhas, svāhā!

At a later time, having failed to perform the protection and auspicious rite by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells (*mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī*), he wandered about—greedy for sensual pleasures, attached, intoxicated with pride, deluded, fainting, and agitated—along with many young female forest peacocks, going from grove to grove, from garden to garden, and from the side of one mountain to the side of another; and through the power of negligence, he entered a certain mountain cleft.

There, for a long time, he was bound by hostile enemies, adversaries, and harmful foes who were watching for a weakness and seeking an opportunity to strike him down with peacock-nooses. While situated in the midst of those enemies, he regained his mindfulness and brought to mind this very Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī:
"Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha! Homage to the Blessed Lady Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās! It is as follows:"

Hu hu hu hu hu hu, hulu hulu hulu, nāga le le le, dumba le le le, nāga le le le, huya huya, vija vija, thusu thusu, gulu gulu, hu cejini, agalu, elā melā, ili melā, tili melā, ili mitte tili mitte, ili tili mitte, dumbe sudumbe, tosu tosu, golā velā capalā vimalā, iṭṭiri bhiṭṭiri riṭṭiri, homage to the Buddhas. Homage to Cilikisi and Godohikā.
Homage to the Arhats! O Hāla-dāla, may the god rain down upon all sides in the ten directions! Homage to the Buddhas! Svāhā!

Then, liberated from that calamity, he reached his own territory in safety and well-being. And he recited these mantra-words: Homage to the Buddha; homage to the Dharma; homage to the Saṅgha; homage to Suvarṇāvabhāsa, the king of peacocks; homage to Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās. It is as follows:

O accomplished one, perfectly purified one; O liberator, grantress of liberation; O released one, utterly freed one; O stainless one, pure one, immaculate one; O dark-blue one, pale-white one; O auspicious one, source of auspiciousness; O golden one, womb of gold; O jewel, womb of jewels; O blessed one, most blessed one, universally blessed one; O accomplisher of all aims, accomplisher of the ultimate aim; O pacifier of all misfortunes, accomplisher of all auspiciousness, warder-off of all inauspiciousness; O mental one, of the mind, great mental one; O marvelous one, exceedingly marvelous one; O released one, liberator, grantress of liberation.

O Acyute, Araje Viraje, Vimale, Amṛte, Amare, Amaraṇi, Brahme, Brahmasvare, Pūrṇe, Pūrṇamanorathe, Mṛtasaṃjīvani, Śrībhadre, Candre, Candraprabhe, Sūrye, Sūryakānte, Vītabhaye, Suvarṇe, Brahmaghoṣe, Brahmakeṣṭhe, Sarvatrāpratihate! Protect, protect me and all sentient beings, svāhā! Homage to all Buddhas! May there be well-being for the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings.
May they live for a hundred years; may they see a hundred autumns. That is to say: tadyathā.

*huci guci muci svāhā*. Furthermore, Ānanda, you might think that at that time, on that occasion, there was another who was the peacock king named Suvarṇāvabhāsa; however, it should not be viewed in this way. Why is that? Because at that time, on that occasion, I myself was the peacock king named Suvarṇāvabhāsa. And now, Ānanda, I shall explain the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells (*mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī*). It is as follows:

ili mitti, tili mitti, tili mili mitti, tili mile, mili tili mitti, cili mili mili, cili mili mili, tili mili, sutumbā tumbā, suvaca cilikisiya, bhinna meḍi. Homage to the Buddhas! Cilikisi, whose root has been reached; itihārā, whose root is red; tumbā sutumbā, kuṭṭi kunaṭṭi, tila kuñja naṭṭi; in Aḍakavātyā, may the god rain for nine months, ten months!

Ili mili kili mili keli mili, ketumūle, dudumbe sudumbe, sudumoḍe, dalime santuvaṭṭe busavaṭṭe, vusara vusara, dhanavastrake, narkalā narkalime, khalime ghoṣe rakhile iti, sajjale, tumbe sutumbe, aṭṭe naṭṭe pranaṭṭe aṇanaṭṭe, anamāle. May the god rain from all sides and everywhere with fresh water! O Nārāyaṇī, Pārāyaṇī, Haritāli, Kuntāli, ili misti, kili misti, ili kili misti, may these be accomplished for me! O Drāmiḍa mantra-words, svāhā!

"This, Ānanda, is the heart of the Queen Mahāmāyūrī. And this, Ānanda, the Queen of Spells Mahāmāyūrī, should be brought to mind by one who has gone to a village; it should be brought to mind by one who has gone to the forest; it should be brought to mind by one on a path, by one on a wrong path, by one in the midst of a royal court, by one in the midst of thieves, by one in the midst of fire, by one in the midst of water, by one in the midst of adversaries, by one in the midst of an assembly, by one in the midst of a dispute, by one bitten by a snake, or by one who has drunk poison."

It should be brought to mind when all fears converge; it should be brought to mind by one who is feverish. When afflicted by any one of the four hundred and four diseases—those arising from wind, bile, phlegm, or their combination—or when various misfortunes have arisen, it should be brought to mind. Why is that?

Ānanda, even one deserving of execution is released from the punishment; one deserving of punishment is released by a beating; one deserving of a beating is released by verbal abuse; one deserving of verbal abuse is released by a reprimand; and one deserving of a reprimand is released by a mere hair-raising exclamation—even so is he released. Furthermore, there shall be the cessation of all his diseases. And these, Ānanda, mantra-words of knowledge should be brought to mind. They are as follows:

Cili mili kili mili ketumūle buddhavarṇe vusaraṇe vusaraṇe, vudāraṇi vudāraṇi, kevaṭṭe kevaṭṭakamūle, iti savale, tuṃbe tuṃbe, perform what is pleasing; O Āvartta, O Parivartta, may the god rain down with fresh water on all sides. Homage to the Blessed One, to Iṭṭittā, to Indragomisikā, to Āśane, Pāśane, Pāpanikūle, Kapilamitte, Ili mitte. Homage to the Blessed Buddha! May these mantra-words be effective for me and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

And by this, Ānanda, Great Peacock Queen of Spells spoken by the Tathāgata, provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns.

Ānanda, I do not perceive anyone in the world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods, humans, and asuras, who—when protected, guarded, rescued, embraced, and preserved by this Great Peacock Queen of Spells, and through this rite of peace, auspiciousness, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth—could [cause them any harm].

or with the intent to cause harm. Whether it be a god, or goddesses, or a son of a god, or a daughter of a god, or an elder god, or an elder goddess, or a member of the divine assembly, or a female member of the divine assembly; or a nāga, or nāgīs, or a son of a nāga, or a daughter of a nāga, or an elder nāga, or an elder nāgī, or a member of the nāga assembly, or a female member of the nāga assembly; or an asura, or asurīs, or a son of an asura, or a daughter of an asura, or an elder asura, or an elder asurī, or a member of the asura assembly...

or an asura attendant or an asura attendantess, or a marut, or a marutī, or a son of a marut, or a daughter of a marut, or a marut elder, or a marut elderess, or a marut attendant, or a marut attendantess; or a garuḍa, or a garuḍī, or a son of a garuḍa, or a daughter of a garuḍa, or a garuḍa elder, or a garuḍa elderess, or a garuḍa attendant, or a garuḍa attendantess; or a gandharva, or a gandharvī, or a son of a gandharva, or a daughter of a gandharva, or a gandharva elder...

or a Gandharva elder, or a member of the Gandharva assembly, or a female member of the Gandharva assembly; or a Kinnara, or a Kinnarī, or a Kinnara son, or a Kinnara daughter, or a Kinnara elder, or a Kinnara elder woman, or a member of the Kinnara assembly, or a female member of the Kinnara assembly; or a Mahoraga, or a Mahoragī, or a Mahoraga son, or a Mahoraga daughter, or a Mahoraga elder, or a Mahoraga elder woman, or a member of the Mahoraga assembly, or a female member of the Mahoraga assembly; or a Yakṣa...

Whether it be a yakṣa, a yakṣa-son, a yakṣa-daughter, a yakṣa elder, a yakṣa elder-woman, a yakṣa attendant, or a yakṣa attendant-woman; or a rākṣasa, a rākṣasī, a rākṣasa-son, a rākṣasa-daughter, a rākṣasa elder, a rākṣasa elder-woman, a rākṣasa attendant, or a rākṣasa attendant-woman; or a preta, a pretī, a preta-son, a preta-daughter, a preta elder, a preta elder-woman, or a preta attendant.

Or a female attendant of a preta, or a piśāca, or a piśācī, or a son of a piśāca, or a daughter of a piśāca, or an elder male piśāca, or an elder female piśāca, or a male attendant of a piśāca, or a female attendant of a piśāca; or a bhūta, or a bhūtī, or a son of a bhūta, or a daughter of a bhūta, or an elder male bhūta, or an elder female bhūta, or a male attendant of a bhūta, or a female attendant of a bhūta; or a kumbhāṇḍa, or a kumbhāṇḍī, or a son of a kumbhāṇḍa, or a daughter of a kumbhāṇḍa, or an elder male kumbhāṇḍa...

Whether it be an old male *kumbhāṇḍa*, a retainer of the *kumbhāṇḍas*, or a female retainer of the *kumbhāṇḍas*; or a *pūtana*, a female *pūtana*, a son of a *pūtana*, a daughter of a *pūtana*, an old male *pūtana*, an old female *pūtana*, a retainer of the *pūtanās*, or a female retainer of the *pūtanās*; or a *kaṭapūtana*, a female *kaṭapūtana*, a son of a *kaṭapūtana*, a daughter of a *kaṭapūtana*, an old male *kaṭapūtana*, an old female *kaṭapūtana*, a retainer of the *kaṭapūtanās*, or a female retainer of the *kaṭapūtanās*; or a *skanda*...

Or a Skanda, or a son of Skanda, or a daughter of Skanda, or an elder Skanda, or an elder female Skanda, or a retainer of Skanda, or a female retainer of Skanda; or an Unmāda, or a female Unmāda, or a son of Unmāda, or a daughter of Unmāda, or an elder Unmāda, or an elder female Unmāda, or a retainer of Unmāda, or a female retainer of Unmāda; or a Chāya, or a female Chāya, or a son of Chāya, or a daughter of Chāya, or an elder Chāya, or an elder female Chāya.

Whether it be a male shadow-attendant or a female shadow-attendant, an epilepsy-demon or an epilepsy-demoness, a son of an epilepsy-demon or a daughter of an epilepsy-demon, an elderly male epilepsy-demon or an elderly female epilepsy-demon, a male follower of an epilepsy-demon or a female follower of an epilepsy-demon; or whether it be a male ostāraka or a female ostāraka, a son of an ostāraka or a daughter of an ostāraka, an elderly male ostāraka or an elderly female ostāraka, a male follower of an ostāraka or a female follower of an ostāraka—they will approach and attend upon [him].

Seeking an opportunity and searching for an opening, he will find no such opportunity. He shall not stand among the assembly of gods as a god; he shall not stand among the assembly of nāgas as a nāga; he shall not stand among the assembly of asuras as an asura; he shall not stand among the assembly of maruts as a marut; he shall not stand among the assembly of garuḍas as a garuḍa; he shall not stand among the assembly of gandharvas as a gandharva; he shall not stand among the assembly of kinnaras as a kinnara; he shall not stand among the assembly of mahoragas as a mahoraga; he shall not stand among the assembly of yakṣas as a yakṣa.

He has no place among the Rākṣasas in the assembly of Rākṣasas; he has no place among the Pretas in the assembly of Pretas; he has no place among the Piśācas in the assembly of Piśācas; he has no place among the Bhūtas in the assembly of Bhūtas; he has no place among the Kumbhāṇḍas in the assembly of Kumbhāṇḍas; he has no place among the Pūtanas in the assembly of Pūtanas; he has no place among the Kaṭapūtanas in the assembly of Kaṭapūtanas; he has no place among the Skandas in the assembly of Skandas; he has no place among the Unmādas in the assembly of Unmādas; nor among the Apasmāras.

There is no place for one who has not restrained his senses; one who has not restrained his senses will find no standing ground. And whoever shall transgress this great vidyā, his head shall split into seven pieces like the cluster of blossoms on an arjuka tree. Furthermore, these mantra-words should be brought to mind here: namely—

*ili mili, kili mili, kili kiṃ dugdhe, mukte sumukte, ūḍa nāḍa sunāḍa, may the god rain upon Paramaḍakavatī, ārā pārā godohikā, ili mili bhijjilikā udukā ḍadukā karoḍukā ili mili tili mili; having performed [this] on all sides, hulu hulu hili hili, mili mili mili mili, pili pili pili pili, kili kili, let it rain from the head, culu culu, cala cala, cili cili, ciḍi ciḍi ciḍi ciḍi.*

Śikhi śikhi śikhi śikhi, juhu juhu juhu juhu juhu juhu juhu juhu juhu juhu, hara hara haraṇe, jaṃbhe prajaṃbhe, jaṃbhe prajaṃbhe of all the wicked and malicious ones; I perform protection, guarding, rescue, embracing, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, and the binding of boundaries for the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings.
And I perform the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years, may he see a hundred autumns. That is to say:

Citramūle citre citramāle, hale halamāle, phale phalamāle, hale hale, māle māle, khulu khulu vuru varuṇo, dhīre dharya, suru suru, the poison is destroyed, the poison is struck down! By the splendor of all the Buddhas, [the poison] of all the wicked and malicious ones—the fang-poison, root-poison, and food-poison—is destroyed; there is no poison! By the seven perfectly enlightened Buddhas: suru suru ke, cara cara ke, biri biri, the poison is destroyed; there is no poison!

By the power of [the Buddha] together with the community of disciples: Ela melā, ili melā, tili melā, tiha duha tilimā timā dumā, vimadhu sukumbhā sumbhā tumbā samatumbā, āḍe nāḍe, tila kuñjanāḍe; may the god rain! O Tilikisi, throughout the nine months on all sides! May there be loving-kindness toward all beings! Vuśaḍe śavariṇi vudāriṇi vudāriṇi, kevaṭṭe kevaṭṭakamūle itiśabare, tuṃbe tuṃbe, make it dear! Āvaṭṭa parivaṭṭa, by means of the new water!

May the Lord rain down on every side! Homage to the Blessed One, Indragomisikā, the Worshipped, Godohikā, Bhṛṅgārikā; Ale Tale Kuntale; Aṭṭe Naṭṭe Kunaṭṭe Āśane Pāśane; Pāpanikūle Pratikūle! Homage to the Blessed Buddhas! May the words of the mantra be effective, svāhā!
Relying upon the Aśoka tree, the Jina Vipaśyin [attained awakening];
the Jina Śikhin at the root of the Puṇḍarīka.
Having approached the foot of a *śāla* tree, Viśvabhū [attained enlightenment];
at the foot of a *śirīṣa* tree, Krakucchanda the Brahmin; and Kanakamuni Buddha at an *udumbara* tree.
Having approached the foot of the nyagrodha tree, Kāśyapa [attained his goal];
having approached the foot of the aśvattha tree, the Sage Gotama, the bull among the Śākyas, attained perfect enlightenment.
Among these Buddhas of great supernatural power,
there are deities who are exceedingly devoted.
May those deities, joyful in mind and exultant, always perform peace and auspiciousness.
Namely as follows:

Ili mili, kili mili, cili kili voli, udumbare, sudumoḍe, busara busara, hu hu, karañje karañjamūle; thus, Sanatā Kuntari Kuntāri, Nārāyaṇi Pārāyaṇi, Paśyani paśya paśya Kapilavastuni; iḍivā iḍivā irivā, may these Dravidian mantra-words be effective—svāhā!

Furthermore, Ānanda, these great medicinal herbs were spoken by Brahmā Sahāpati, by Śakra, the lord of the gods, by the four Great Kings, and by the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals. For anyone, Ānanda, who should approach with a malicious mind while the names of these great medicinal herbs are being recited, his head shall split into seven pieces like the cluster of blossoms on an arjaka tree. It is just as follows:

At the root of the *kīrtti*, at the root of the *era*, at the root of the *eraṇḍa*, at the root of the *samanta*; at the *aḍanāḍa* and the *kuśanāḍa*; at the *itte* and the *mitte*; at the *pāru*, the *aḍakā*, and the *maraḍakā*; at the *ilikiśi*, the *godohikā*, the *udbandha*, the *mābhibhinna*, and the *medā*. Homage to the Buddhas! May there be well-being for you bipeds; may there be well-being for you quadrupeds;
may there be well-being for those traveling on the road, and well-being for those who have returned.
May there be well-being at night, may there be well-being by day, and may there be well-being when midday has arrived;
may there be well-being for you everywhere, and may no evil come upon you. May all days be auspicious, and may all constellations be favorable.
All Buddhas possess great supernatural power, and all Arhats are free from outflows;
by this declaration of truth, may there be well-being in every direction.

By means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās spoken by the Tathāgata, provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns.

And those yakṣas and mahāyakṣas, Ānanda, who dwell on the shores of the ocean; those who are on Sumeru, the king of mountains, and those on other kings of mountains; those in forests and great forests, in rivers and great rivers, in groves and great groves, in vineyards, ponds, and pools; in mountain caves and cemeteries, at crossroads and great crossroads, at four-way junctions and triple junctions; in towns and great cities, in hamlets and villages, in parks, woods, and groves; on paths and byways—those who...

And Ānanda, those yakṣas and mahāyakṣas who dwell in the royal capital of Aḍakavatī—may they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of vidyās, provide protection, guarding, rescue, acceptance, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns.
It is as follows: tadyathā.

*Hari hāriṇi, cali cālini, tramaṇi trāmaṇi, mohanī stambhani jambhani, svayaṃbhuve svāhā!* In the eastern direction, O Ānanda, there dwells the great Gandharva king named Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he is the sovereign of the Gandharvas, surrounded by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of Gandharvas, and exercises lordship over the Gandharvas.

Whoever protects and guards the eastern direction—may he, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, army commanders, servants, messengers, preeminent men, and retinue, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of vidyās, provide protection, defense, rescue, shelter, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, and the destruction of poison for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings.

May he perform the binding of the boundary and the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. That is to say: *suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru me svāhā*.

Ānanda, in the southern direction there dwells the great king of the kumbhāṇḍas named Virūḍhaka, the lord of the kumbhāṇḍas, who presides over the sovereignty of the kumbhāṇḍas with a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of kumbhāṇḍas.

Whoever protects and guards the southern direction—may he, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, army commanders, servants, messengers, preeminent men, and retinue, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, Queen of Vidyās, provide protection, defense, rescue, shelter, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, and the binding of boundaries for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings.
And let him perform the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years, may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:
*veluke veluke amitraghātanī varuṇavati somavati veṇumālini veluni putrike co cū ci cū svāhā*.
Ānanda, in the western direction dwells the great king of the nāgas named Virūpākṣa; a lord of nāgas with a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of nāgas, he exercises sovereignty over the nāgas.

He who protects and guards the western direction—may he too, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, army commanders, servants, messengers, preeminent men, and retinue, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, Queen of Spells, provide protection, defense, rescue, shelter, peace, well-being, exemption from punishment, exemption from weapons, the neutralization of poison, and the destruction of poison for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings.

May he perform the binding of the boundary and the binding of the earth! May he live for a hundred years, may he see a hundred autumns! It is as follows: veduri veduri veduri veduri, maṭṭite maṭṭite, koṭi koṭi, vidyumati, hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu, cu cu cu cu cu cu cu cu, ru ru ru ru ru ru ru ru, ca ca ca ca ca ca ca ca, sa svāhā.

In the northern direction, Ānanda, there dwells the great Yakṣa king named Vaiśravaṇa, the lord of Yakṣas, who, surrounded by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of Yakṣas, exercises sovereignty over the Yakṣas.

He who protects and guards the northern direction—may he, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, army commanders, servants, messengers, preeminent men, and retinue, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of vidyās, provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, and the binding of boundaries for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings.
And let him perform the binding of the earth! May he live for a hundred years, may he see a hundred autumns! That is to say:
*sori sori, siri siri, mati mati, hiri hiri, mati pele mati pele, piṅgale curu curu, hataṃ viṣaṃ, bandhumati, nihataṃ viṣaṃ bandhumati svāhā*.
To the east is Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and to the south is Virūḍhaka.
In the west is Virūpākṣa, and Kubera guards the northern direction.
These four great kings, the illustrious guardians of the world, possessing vast armies and great power, protect the four directions.
They crush the armies of enemy factions; they are invincible and unconquerable.
Possessing supernatural powers, radiance, beauty, and fame, these beings of great majesty even engage in battle against the gods and asuras.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells, provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows: *tadyathā.*

Mele, kile, tile, mile, śile, vāse, duṃbe duṃbe, may the god rain on all sides! Hili mili tuṃbe tuṃbe, aṭṭa vaṭṭa paradu vattā, may the god rain! Guḍa guḍantu on all sides within Āḍakovatī! Aṇḍe maṇḍe tunde tutunde curke vukke, iriḍi miriḍi niriḍi ciriḍi, hili hili, hulu hulu, mili mili, tule tatale svāhā! Take up, Ānanda, the names of the great yakṣa generals who dwell upon the earth.
The eldest son of Kubera, Saṃjaya, who is borne by men, dwells in Mithilā; he is one who makes true offerings to the gods.

May he also, by means of this great Mahāmāyūrī Queen of Spells, perform protection for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may he provide guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns. *Bale balkale, mātaṅgi caṇḍāli puruṣa, nici nici nigauri gandhāre, caṇḍāli mātaṅgi, mālini hili hili, āgati gati, gauri gandhāri kauṣṭhikā vacari vihāri, hili hili, kuñje svāhā!* *Krakucchanda is in Pāṭaliputra; Aparājita is at Ṣṭhalā;
Śaila is in Bhadrapura; and Mānava is the Yakṣa in the north.*
Vajrapāṇi, who has made his abode on Vulture Peak in Rājagṛha,
circles this earth and its oceans three times;
he is of great strength and great majesty, with a stride spanning ten yojanas.
The yakṣa Garuḍa is at Vipula; Citragupta is at Citīmukha; and at Rājagṛha is the yakṣa Vakkula, who possesses a great army and great power.
The two Yakṣas Kāla and Upakāla dwell in Kapilavastu,
where the Sage, the Buddha, the banner of the Śākyas, the Great Muni, was born. Maheśvara, as Kalmāṣapāda, dwells among the Kirātas in Vairā.
Bṛhaspati shall dwell in Śrāvastī, and Sāgara in Sāketa; Vajrāyudha in Vaiśālī, and Haripiṅgala among the Mallas; Mahākāla in Vārāṇasī, and Sudarśana in Campā.
Viṣṇu is the yakṣa in Dvārakā; Dharaṇa is in Dvārapālī;
Vibhūṣana is in Tāmraparṇī; and Mardana is in Uragā. Āṭavaka is the yakṣa in Āṭavī; Kapila is in Bahudhanyaka.
Vasutrāta dwells in Ujjayinī;
Vasubhūmi in Avanti; Bharuka in Bharukaccha; Nanda resides in Nandapura; Mālyadhara is in Agrodaka; and Ānanda is on Mount Amara.
Śukladaṃṣṭra shall rule over Suvāstu; Dṛḍha by name shall rule over the Manasvinas;
Mahāgiri shall rule over Girinagara; and Vāsava shall rule over Vaidiśa. In Rohitaka, Kārttikeya, the world-renowned Kumāra, shall reside.
Śatabāhu was in Varṇabhaṭa; Vṛhadratha was among the Kaliṅgas;
Duryodhana was in Śrughna; Arjuna was in Arjunavana; the Yakṣa Maṇḍapa was in Mardana; and Girikūṭa was in Mālava.
Bhadra was among the Rohitāśvas; Sarvabhadra was in the ocean;
Pālitaka was the caravan leader in Saṇṭīraka;
Dhaneśvara [was] in [the city of] Vasāti; and Kūṭadaṃṣṭra was in Ajitañjaya.
Śiva is in the capital of Śivapura, and Śivabhadra is in Bhīṣaṇa;
Indra is in Indrapura, and the Yakṣa Puṣpaketu is in Śilāpura.
Dāruka dwells in Dārukapura; Kapila resides among the Varṇins; Maṇibhadra and his brother Pūrṇabhadra are in Brahmavatī; Pramardana is in Gāndhāra, and Prabhañjana is in Takṣaśilā.
The great yakṣa Kharoṣṭa dwells on Mount Daśaśaila;
Trigupta is on the banks of the Hanumat, and Prabhaṃkara is in Rauruka. Nandī and Vardhana are both in the city of Nandivardhana.
Vāyira is in Vāyibhūmi; Laṃpāka is fond of quarreling;
Gardabhaka is in Mathurā; Kolaśodara is in Laṅkā;
the Yakṣa Sūryaprabha is in Śūnya; and Girimuṇḍa is in Kośala.
Vijaya and Vaijayanta dwell in Pāṇḍumāthura;
the Yakṣa Pūrṇaka is in Malaya, and the Kinnara is in Kerala.
Meghamālin is in Pauṇḍra, and Khaṇḍaka is in Pratiṣṭhāna.
In Pitaṅgala there was Śaṅkālī; in Taraṅgavatī, Sukhāvaha;
in Nāsika, the Yakṣa Sundara; in Tarukacchaka, Āsaṅga; in Nandika, Pitānandin; and in Karahāṭaka, Vīra.
Lambodara was among the Kaliṅgas, Mahābhuja in Kauśalyā,
Svastika in Svastikaṭaka, and Pālaka in Vanavāsī.
Bhadrakarṇa was at Taṭiskandha, and Dhanavara in Ṣaḍapura.
In Vairāmaka there is the yakṣa Bala; in Avanti, Priyadarśana; in Gomardana, Śikhaṇḍin; and in Vaideśa, Aṅgulipriya. (Mmk 21)
In Tripurī, there is Veṣṭitaka, who is like an umbrella;
in Makaranda, there is Ekakakṣa; in Udumbara, there are Viśālākṣa and Aṇḍabha; in Vaiśālī, there is Anābhoga; and in Śāntivatī, there is Virocana.
Caritaka was at Ahicchatra, and likewise Kapila at Kampilya;
Bakkula was at Ujjayinī, and likewise Pūrṇaka at Maṇḍavyā;
Naigameśa was at Pāñcālī, and Prasabha at Gajasāhvaya.
In Varuṇā were Dṛḍhadhanus and Purañjaya of the Yodheya clan;
in Kurukṣetra were the two Yakṣa lords Taraka and Kurutara, and right there were the two renowned Yakṣīs Mahollūkhala and Mekhalā.
Vyatipātana, Siddhārtha, Āyatīva, and Anivāsina;
likewise Siddhapātra in Śrughna, and Sthala in Sthala.
Furthermore, there are the two Yakṣas Siṃhabala and Vyāghrabalābala.
Koṭivarṣa and Mahāsena are in Parapuraṃjaya;
Puṣpadanta is in Campā and Magadha is in Girivraja; the Yakṣa Parvata is in Goyoga and Susena is in Nāgara.
Vīrabāhu was in Sāketa, Sukhāvaha in Kākaṭī, Anāyasa in Kauśāmbī, and Bhadrika in Bhadrikā;
likewise, the yakṣa named Bhūtamukha was in Pāṭaliputra.
Aśoka was among the Kāñcīs; Kaṭaṅkaṭa among the Ambaṣṭhas; Siddhārtha in Bharukaccha; Mandaka in Ajitañjaya;
Mañjakeśa in Agrodaka; and Maṇikānana in Saindhava.
And those Yakṣas who dwell in Kapilavastu— Vikaṭa and Kaṭa— as well as Naikṛtika in Gāndhāraka, and Dvāraka in Nila-yadhruva.
The yakṣa Madhyamakīya is in Mahāyaśas, the daughter of Subhadrā; Vairāṭaka is in Sārapura, and Jambhaka is in the Marubhūmis.
The yakṣa known as Vṛndakaṭa is there, as well as the one called Vikaṭa.
Vemānika dwells among the gods, Mandara among the Daradas; Prabhankara is in Kaśmīra and Campaka in Jaṭāpura;
and he who is known by the name Pāñcika resides among the Sindhus.
He who has five hundred sons, a great army, and immense strength— Pāñcika’s eldest son— dwells in the lands of Cīna. His brother, known by the name Skandhākṣa, dwells in Kauśika.
Uṣṭrapāda is in Kaliṅga; Maṇḍala is in Maṇḍalāsana; the Lord of Laṅkā is in Kāpiśī; Mārīci is in Rāmakāṅkṣī;
Dharmapāla is in Khāśa; and Mahābhuja is indeed in Bahlika.
The illustrious Prince Jinarṣabha, son of Vaiśravaṇa,
surrounded by ten million yakṣas, resides among the Tukhāras;
Sātāgiri and Haimavata dwell by the Sindhu and the ocean.
Triśūlapāṇi dwells in Tripura; Pramardana in Kaliṅga;
Pāñcālagaṇḍa in Dramiḍa; Dhaneśvara in Siṃhala; Śukāmukha in the forest; and Kiṃkara dwells in Pātāla.
Prabhāsvara dwells in Puṇḍarīka, Samila in Mahāpura, Prabhañjana among the Daradas, and Piṅgala resides in Ambulima.
Vaccaḍa is in Uccaḍādhāna, and Mātali indeed in Kāmade.
Suprabuddha is at Putrīvaṭa; Narakuvera is in Kāpiśī; Pārāsara is among the Pāratas; and Śaṅkara is in the Śaka settlements.
Vemacitra was in Bāhlīka, Piṅgala among the Ketakas;
Pūrṇamukha was in Puṇḍravardhana, and Karāṭa in Oḍiyānaka;
Kumbhodara was among the Kauśalas, and Makaradhvaja in the Maru country.
Citrasena resides in Vokkāna, Rāvaṇa in Ramatha, Piṅgala in Rāśina, and Priyadarśana in Patnīya;
while the yakṣa Kumbhīra dwells in this vast city of Rājagṛha.
Furthermore, he is attended by hundreds of thousands of yakṣas.
In Ahicchatrā he is Gopāla; in Alakāpurī he is Alaka; in Nandinagara he is Nandi; and in Grāmaghoṣa Bali resides.
At the descent of the gods, Vaiśravaṇa was the protector of his own army; surrounded by ten million yakṣas, he resided in Aḍakavatī.
These yakṣas possess great supernatural power, vast armies, and great strength.
They crush the armies of adversaries, being invincible and unconquerable.
Possessing supernatural powers, radiance, beauty, and fame,
these beings of great majesty even engage in battle with the gods and asuras.

May they also, by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells, provide protection, defense, rescue, guardianship, preservation, peace, well-being, exemption from punishment, exemption from weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Akaṭe vikaṭe hariṇi hāriṇi dharaṇi dhāraṇi, hukke hukke, vukke vukke, hana hana hana hana hana hana hana hana hana hana, [strike] my enemies and those of all sentient beings; daha daha daha daha daha daha daha daha daha, [burn] those who wish me ill and those who wish ill to all sentient beings; paca paca paca paca paca paca paca paca paca paca, [cook] my adversaries and those of all sentient beings; dhu dhu.

Dhu dhu dhu dhu dhu dhu dhu dhu! Destroy those who wish me harm! Hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu! Jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi jiṭi! Destroy my enemies and those of all sentient beings! Culu culu culu culu culu culu culu culu culu culu culu! Hili hili hili hili hili hili hili hili hili hili! Mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili! Phuru phuru phuru!

Phuru phuru phuru phuru phuru phuru phuru, ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi ciṭi, destroy all my enemies and those of all sentient beings! Hikke mikke cikke cukke Śrībhadre Maṅgale Samantabhadre Hiraṇyagarbhe, O accomplisher of all aims! Amale Vimalē, Candre Candraprabhe, Sūrye Sūryaprabhe Sūryakānte, Durvijñeye Duṃbe Duṃbe Doduṃbe, Priyaṃkare, protect me and all sentient beings; may they live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns!
"Ānanda, you should take up the names of the great yakṣa generals who guard and protect the ten directions.
Ānanda, in the eastern direction there dwell four great yakṣa generals who guard and protect the eastern direction. They are as follows: Dīrgha, Sunetra, Pūrṇaka, and Kapila."

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī Queen of Vidyās, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Ānanda, in the southern direction there dwell four great yakṣa generals who guard and protect the southern direction. They are as follows: Siṃha, Upasiṃha, Śaṅkhila, and Nanda.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī Queen of Spells, provide protection, defense, rescue, guardianship, preservation, peace, and well-being for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may they provide immunity from punishment, immunity from weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Ānanda, in the western direction there dwell four great yakṣa generals who guard and protect the western direction. They are as follows: Hari, Harikeśa, Prabhu, and Piṅgala.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī Queen of Spells, provide protection, defense, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Ānanda, in the northern direction there dwell four great yakṣa generals who guard and protect the northern direction. They are as follows: Dharaṇa, Dharaṇanda, Udyogapāla, and Viṣṇu.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī Queen of Spells, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

Ānanda, there are these four great yakṣa generals who dwell in the intermediate directions; they guard and protect the intermediate directions. They are as follows: Pañcika, Pañcālagaṇḍa, Sātāgiri, and Haimavata.

May they also, by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells (*mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī*), provide protection, guarding, rescue, acceptance, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Ānanda, there are these four great yakṣa generals who dwell upon the earth; they protect and guard the beings who have gone to the earth. They are as follows: Bhūma, Subhūma, Kāla, and Upakāla.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

Ānanda, there are these four great yakṣa generals who dwell in the atmosphere; they protect and guard sentient beings who have gone into the atmosphere. They are as follows: Sūrya, Soma, Agni, and Vāyu.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells, provide protection, guarding, rescue, acceptance, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

"Ānanda, you should take up the names of the Dharma-brothers of the great king Vaiśravaṇa, those who protect and guard sentient beings; they destroy calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions for all beings, and they wander through the world for the sake of benefiting the world. They are as follows:"

Indra, Soma, Sūrya, Varuṇa, Prajāpati, Bharadvāja, Īśana, Candana, Kāma, Śreṣṭha, Kunikaṇṭha, Nikaṇṭhaka, Vaḍi, Maṇi, Māṇicara, Praṇāda, Upapañcaka, Sātāgiri, Haimavata, Pūrṇaka, Khadira, Kovida, Gopālayakṣa, Āṭavaka, Nararāja, Jinarṣabha, Pāñcālagaṇḍa, Sumukha, Dīrghayakṣa together with his retinue, Citrasena the Gandharva, Triphālī, Trikhaṇṭhaka, Dīrghaśakti, and Mātali.

These yakṣas, great yakṣas, leaders of the army, endowed with supernatural power, splendor, beauty, and fame, are the righteous brothers of the Great King Vaiśravaṇa. To whomsoever the Great King Vaiśravaṇa declares, "This yakṣa of mine is harassing me; this one does not leave me," these righteous brothers of the Great King Vaiśravaṇa shall likewise provide protection by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās, for the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings.

May they provide protection, refuge, shelter, and guardianship; peace, well-being, the avoidance of punishment, and the avoidance of weapons; the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

May they protect us from the strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes of the Kali age; may they protect us from the seizure of humans, the seizure of non-humans, the seizure of gods, the seizure of *nāgas*, the seizure of *asuras*, the seizure of *maruts*, the seizure of *garuḍas*, the seizure of *gandharvas*, the seizure of *kiṃnaras*, the seizure of *mahoragas*, the seizure of *yakṣas*, the seizure of *rākṣasas*, the seizure of *pretas*, the seizure of *piśācas*, the seizure of *bhūtas*, the seizure of *kumbhāṇḍas*, and the seizure of *pūtanās*.

May they grant me protection from the Kaṭapūtana spirit, from the Skanda spirit, from the Unmāda spirit, from the Chāyā spirit, from the Apasmāra spirit, from the Ostāraka spirit, from the Nakṣatra spirits, and from the Lepaka spirits.

From those who take away vitality, from those who take away blood, from those who take away fat, from those who take away flesh, from those who take away marrow, (Mmk Taku 28) from those who take away birth, from those who take away life, from those who take away strength, from those who take away garlands, from those who take away perfumes, from those who take away flowers, from those who take away fruits, from those who take away crops, from those who take away oblations, from those who take away pus, from those who take away blood, from those who take away excrement, from those who take away urine, from those who take away saliva, from those who take away phlegm, and from those who take away nasal mucus.

May [the deities] protect me, the monk Svāti, and all sentient beings from those who consume vomit, those who consume excrement, those who consume impurities, and those who consume flowing fluids; may they provide guard, rescue, and refuge for me and all sentient beings, and may they grant us acceptance, protection, peace, well-being, the avoidance of punishment, the avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; [protect us] from sorcery, from *kākhorda* spells, from incantations, from oblations, from oblations with fire, and from madness.

May they protect me and all sentient beings from spirits, from *vetāḍas*, from the assault of the mind, from servitude, from ill-eaten food, from indigestion, from evil shadows, from the sight of the hideous, from the sight of the poorly drawn, from the sight of the poorly leaped, from the sight of the poorly shaken, from terror, from portents, from epilepsy, from fright, and from demons.

May they provide protection from fear of kings, fear of thieves, fear of fire, fear of water, fear of enemy armies, fear of famine, fear of lightning, fear of untimely death, fear of earthquakes, fear of creditors, fear of fierce wild beasts, fear of enemies, and fear of death—from all fears. May they protect me, the monk Svāti, and all sentient beings from the fear of ringworm, itching, leprosy, fistula, hemorrhoids, scabies, pustules, eczema, erysipelas, and jaundice. May they remove the pain of headaches.

May they remove hemiplegia, loss of appetite, eye disease, nose disease, mouth disease, throat disease, heart disease, constriction of the throat, earache, toothache, pain in the heart, pain in the sides, pain in the back, pain in the abdomen, pain in the cheek, pain in the thighs, pain in the anus, pain in the vulva, pain in childbirth, pain in the thighs, pain in the calves, pain in the hands, pain in the feet, and pain in the major and minor limbs; may they remove fever.

May they destroy the fever that recurs every day, every two days, every three days, every four days, every seven days, every half-month, every month, every two months, or every moment; the constant fever, the irregular fever, the fever caused by *bhūtas*, the fever caused by *pretas*, the fever caused by humans, and the fever caused by non-humans; the fever arising from wind, bile, phlegm, or their combination; all fevers, all diseases, all seizing spirits, all poisons, all evils, and all fears—may they destroy these for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings.
*Svāhā*.

"Ānanda, there are these twelve great piśācīs by whom the Bodhisattva was protected while in his mother’s womb, protected as he was being born, and protected once he was born. What are those twelve? They are as follows:

Lambā, Pralambā, Vilambā, Olambā, Hārītī, Harikeśī, Piṅgalā, Kālī, Karālī, Kambugrīvā, Kākī, and Kalaśodarī. These twelve great piśācīs are endowed with supernatural power, radiance, beauty, and fame; possessing great majesty, they even participate in the battle between the gods and the asuras."

May these [beings] also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns. And here are the mantra words: namely—

Hare khare khure male vimale mūle, they rejoice, the intoxicated ones, adorned. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, svāhā! Auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness! For the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

"Ānanda, there are these eight great piśācīs who feed on flesh and blood and harass human beings; by them the Bodhisattva was protected while in his mother’s womb, protected when being born, and protected once he was born. Who, then, are they? They are as follows: Madā, Madanā, Madotkaṭā, Upamadā, the preta Ojohāriṇī, Asanī, and Grasanī. These eight great piśācīs are endowed with supernatural power, radiance, beauty, and fame; possessing great majesty, they even participate in the battle between the gods and the asuras."

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells, provide protection, guarding, rescue, acceptance, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Hare khare! At the root where the hooves of the donkey meet, the adorned ones dance in intoxication. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svasti svasti svasti svasti, for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, svāhā! Svasti svasti svasti svasti. For the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

Furthermore, Ānanda, these seven great piśācīs, who feed on flesh and blood and harass human beings, protected the Bodhisattva while he was in his mother’s womb, protected him as he was being born, and protected him once he was born. Who are they? They are as follows:

Agrodikā, Rakṣitikā, Citrapiśācikā, Pūrṇabhadrikā, Agnirakṣitikā, Mitrakālikā, and Ṛṣirakṣitikā. These seven great piśācīs are endowed with supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), radiance, beauty, and fame; possessing great majesty, they even participate in the battle between the gods and the asuras.

May these [beings] also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of vidyās, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, and well-being for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may they provide the avoidance of punishment, the avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Hare khare khure male mile mūle, the intoxicated Maṇḍitikas rejoice. Hulu hulu hulu hulu (Mmvr Taku 31) hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svasti svasti svasti svasti, svāhā! May there be well-being for the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

Furthermore, Ānanda, there are these five great rākṣasīs by whom the Bodhisattva was protected while in his mother’s womb, protected at birth, and protected even after he was born. Who are they? They are as follows:

Kuṇṭhā, Nikuṇṭhā, Nandā, Viṣṇulā, and Kapilā. These five great rākṣasīs possess supernatural power, radiance, beauty, and fame; being of great majesty, they even participate in the battle between the gods and the asuras.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of vidyās, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Hare khare, at the root where the hooves of the donkey meet, the adorned ones intoxicate themselves with madness. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svāhā! For the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings, svāhā! Auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness! For myself and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

"Ānanda, there are these eight great rākṣasīs who feed on flesh and blood and harass human beings; they protected the Bodhisattva while he was in his mother’s womb, they protected him as he was being born, and they protected him once he was born. Who, then, are they? They are as follows:"

Moha, Susīmā, Kuśākṣī, Keśinī, Kāmbījī, Sumitrā, Lohitākṣī, and Kācarā—these, Ānanda, are the eight great rākṣasīs who feed on flesh and blood. They carry off men, women, boys, and girls; they frequent maternity wards; they follow those going to empty houses or into the darkness; they summon people and steal the vital energy (*ojas*) of humans. These great *kṛtyās* possess no compassion; they terrify the human population.
Thus, these eight great rākṣasīs are possessed of supernatural power, radiance, beauty, and fame; endowed with great majesty, they even participate in the battles between the gods and the asuras.

May these also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells, provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Hare khare khure male mile mūle, the adorned ones rejoice in intoxication. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svāhā! For the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, svāhā! Auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness! For the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

"Ānanda, there are these ten great rākṣasīs by whom the Bodhisattva was protected while in his mother’s womb, protected as he was being born, and protected once he was born. Who, then, are they? They are as follows:

the rākṣasī Hārītī, the rākṣasī Nandā, the rākṣasī Piṅgalā, the rākṣasī Śaṅkhinī, the rākṣasī Kālikā, the rākṣasī Devamitrā, the rākṣasī Kumbhāṇḍā, the rākṣasī Kuntadraṃṣṭrā, the rākṣasī Kambojī, and the rākṣasī Anālā."
Thus, these ten great rākṣasīs are endowed with supernatural power, radiance, beauty, and fame; possessing great majesty, they even participate in the battle between the gods and the asuras.

May these [beings] also, by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells, provide protection, guarding, rescue, acceptance, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Hare khare! At the root where the hooves of the wild donkeys meet, the adorned women become intoxicated. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svāhā for the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings. May there be well-being, well-being, well-being, well-being; svāhā for the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings.
"Ānanda, there are these twelve great rākṣasīs by whom the Bodhisattva was protected while in his mother’s womb, protected at birth, and protected once born. Who are they? They are as follows:

the rākṣasī Anārthikā, the rākṣasī Samudrā, the rākṣasī Raudrā, the rākṣasī Prāṇahāriṇī, the rākṣasī Vidyādharā, the rākṣasī Dhanurdharā, the rākṣasī Śaradharā, the rākṣasī Asidharā, the rākṣasī Haladharā, the rākṣasī Cakradharā, the rākṣasī Cakravāḍā, and the rākṣasī Vibhūṣaṇā."
"Ānanda, these twelve great rākṣasīs are possessed of supernatural power, radiance, beauty, and fame; being of great majesty, they even participate in the battle between the gods and the asuras."

May these [beings] also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī Queen of Spells, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Hare khare! At the root where the hooves of the donkey meet, the adorned ones dance in intoxication. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svāhā! For the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings, svāhā! Auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness, auspiciousness! For the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

Ānanda, there are these twelve great mothers by whom the Bodhisattva was protected while in his mother’s womb, protected as he was being born, and protected once he was born. And those beings who cause harm, affliction, and terror—what are they?
They are as follows: Brāhmī, Raudrī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Aindrī, Vārāhī, Kauverī, Vāruṇī, Yāmyā, Vāyavyā, Āgneyī, and Mahākālī.

May these [deities] also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās, provide protection, guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:

Hare khare khure male mile mūle, the adorned ones rejoice in intoxication. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svāhā! For the monk Svāti, for myself, and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

Ānanda, there is a great piśācī named Ekajaṭā, the wife of Rāvaṇa, who dwells on the shore of the ocean. She roams for eighty thousand yojanas in a single night by the scent of blood. Hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu, lu lu lu lu, meḍi meḍi meḍi meḍi, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, svāhā! By these great vidyās, these great mantras, these great Pratisarās, and these great protections, the *kṛtyas* of the monk Svāti, of myself, and of all sentient beings are destroyed; the magical rites (*karman*) are destroyed; the *kākhordas*, *kiraṇas*, *vetāḍas*, *ciccas*, and *preṣakas* are destroyed; the *skandas*, *unmādas*, *chāyās*, *apasmāras*, and *ostārakas* are destroyed; the terrors (*uttrāsas*), poisons (*garas*), and toxins (*viṣas*) are destroyed; the wasting diseases (*śoṣas*) are destroyed; the ill-eaten, the ill-vomited, and the ill-shaded are destroyed; the ill-gazed upon, the ill-drawn, and the ill-transgressed are destroyed.

The shaken-off and destroyed are all fevers: those occurring every day, every second day, every third day, every fourth day, every seven days, every half-month, every month, daily, momentary, constant, and intermittent; fevers caused by spirits, by wind, by bile, by phlegm, by a combination of humors, human fevers, and non-human fevers are destroyed. All fevers, ringworm, itching, skin eruptions, leprosy, swellings, pustules, scabies, erysipelas, and iron-like discolorations are destroyed. Headaches, hemicrania, loss of appetite, and eye diseases [are destroyed].

Disease of the nose, disease of the mouth, disease of the throat, heart disease, throat obstruction, earache, toothache, heart pain, side pain, back pain, stomach pain, temple pain, bladder pain, anal pain, vaginal pain, labor pain, thigh pain, calf pain, hand pain, foot pain, and pain in the limbs and minor members—all these are destroyed. All seizing spirits, all poisons, and all diseases are destroyed. May there be well-being for me and for all sentient beings.
May there be well-being at night, well-being by day, and well-being when standing at midday.
May all Buddhas grant you well-being throughout every day and night.
Homage be to the Buddha; homage be to Awakening; homage be to the Liberated One; homage be to Liberation.
Homage be to the peaceful one, homage be to peace;
homage to the liberated one, homage to liberation. To those brahmins who have cast off evil qualities, [homage].

Homage to them! May they grant protection to me and to all sentient beings. May there be well-being for my mother; may there be well-being for my father; may there be well-being for the one dwelling in the womb. May there be well-being for bipeds; may there be well-being for quadrupeds; may there be well-being for those with many feet. May there be well-being for those encompassed within the three realms of existence; may there be well-being for me and for all sentient beings, svāhā!

"These and other nāga kings, Ānanda, who from time to time rain upon this circle of the earth, who from time to time thunder, who from time to time flash lightning, and who from time to time bring forth crops."

They behold the Buddha, have undertaken the precepts, and have gone for refuge to the Triple Gem. Long-lived, they remain for an eon; they are liberated from the fear of *garuḍas*, from the fear of tongues of flame, from the fear of royal punishment, and from the fear of earthquakes. Dwelling in great jeweled palaces upon the earth, they are long-lived, of great renown, possessed of great supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*), great majesty, great wealth, and large retinues. They are destroyers of enemy forces, endowed with miraculous power, radiance, beauty, and fame.

Those of great supernatural power even experience battles between gods and asuras. Thus, these nāga kings—along with their sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, army commanders, servants, messengers, leaders, and retinues—by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās, may they provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, and the avoidance of punishment and weapons for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings.

May they perform the purification of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. May there be well-being for me and for all sentient beings! Svāhā!

Whether one is impure or pure, intoxicated or heedless, walking, standing, sitting, lying down, awake, arrived, or not yet arrived—may there be well-being from fear of kings, fear of thieves, fear of fire, fear of water, fear of imprisonment, fear of adversaries, fear of enemies, fear of terror, fear of foreign armies, fear of famine, fear of untimely death, and fear of earthquakes and fierce wild beasts.

May there be well-being from the fear of ringworm, itching, skin spots, leprosy, swellings, pustules, scabies, erysipelas, liver spots, consumption, and terror.
