And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of spells, was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One Vipaśyin. It is as follows:

*araḍe karaḍe maraḍe madavardhane avaśabare ture ture care care śabare parṇaśabare, hucu hucu, kuci kuci, muci muci, huci huci huci huci huci huci huci, muci muci muci muci svāhā*. And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of spells, was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One Śikhin. It is as follows: [as follows...]

*iḍi miḍi khire vikhire, hili hili hili, mili mili, tumūle, ambare ambarāvati, dumbe dumbe hili hili hili, kurvi kurvi kurvi, muci muci muci, svāhā.* And this, Ānanda, is the Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Spells, spoken and approved by the Perfectly Enlightened One Viśvabhū. It is as follows:

Morike morike morike kevaṇṭu maṇḍitike, hare hare hare hare hare hare, ghare ghare, khare khare, phare phare phare, phali nidanti nidantire, śakaṭi makaṭi, naṇḍa naḍini, śiri śiri śiri śiri śiri śiri svāhā. And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One Krakucchanda. It is as follows:

*Hiḍi miḍi kuḍi miḍi, tuḍi kuḍi aḍi muḍi tuḍi tuḍi āḍe dante dantile śakari makāri thagari cagari kañcane kañcanāvati, śabare, bare bare bare bare bare bare, dante siddhi svāhā.* Ānanda, this Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī was spoken and also approved by the Perfectly Awakened One Kanakamuni. It is as follows:

*Tantule tatale tatale calate, tale tale tale tale, vire vijaye vidyādharē, araje araje virajāmāti, mātī mālinī maṇḍe śrīmaṇḍe, jvala jvala jvala jvala jvala jvala, bhadravati siddhi svāhā.* And this, Ānanda, is the Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Spells, spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One Kāśyapa. It is as follows:

Aṇḍare paṇḍare kaṇḍare maṇḍare khaṇḍare jaṃbu juṃbunadi jaṃbuvati, matte maṇḍitike, amare siddhi, hara hara hara hara, paśu paśu paśu paśu paśupati svāhā siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi svāhā. And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, queen of spells, has now been spoken and approved by me as well as by the Perfectly Awakened One, Śākyamuni. It is as follows:

Hili mili kili mili ilile katale ketumūle aḍamali ḍaphe ḍaphe busareke, busaṭṭa narakande katili bocalike kambu dāriṇikāya śabaraṅge tatuṭṭa bharaśebho vardhani prakṛti daṃṣṭra mili tale, īti hāse amale makule baṭṭa baṭṭa varṣantu, devaḥ samantā yathā sukhaṃ daśasu dikṣu. Hili mili kili mili ilile katale ketumūle aḍamali ḍaphe ḍaphe busareke, busaṭṭa narakande katili bocalike kambu dāriṇikāya śabaraṅge tatuṭṭa bharaśebho vardhani prakṛti daṃṣṭra mili tale, īti hāse amale makule baṭṭa baṭṭa may they rain down; O Lord, may you rain everywhere, happily, in the ten directions.

Homage to the Blessed One! May there be water for the white lotus! Homage to the Blessed One Iṭiṭā, Godohikā, Bhṛṅgārikā; Aruci, Maruci, Naṭṭa, Naṭṭa, Vajre, Vajranaṭṭe, Udayanapriye; Ale, Tāle, Kuntāle, Kule, Tāle; Nārāyaṇī, Pārāyaṇī; Paśyani, Sparśani! May the Drāmiḍa mantra-words be effective! Svāhā!

Just as this was spoken and approved by me, Śākyamuni, the perfectly awakened one—when the monk Ānanda performed a rite for well-being for the monk Svāti who had been bitten by a snake—so too let there be protection for all sentient beings; let there be guarding, rescue, embracing, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns.
And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās, was spoken and rejoiced in by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya.

It is as follows: *śiri śiri śiri, bhadre; jyoti jyoti jyoti, bhadre; hare hare hare, hariṇi hāriṇi; danti śabari śive śūlapāṇini; bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi, bodhisatve, bodhiparipācanīye svāhā*.
And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās, was also spoken and rejoiced in by Brahmā Sahāpati. It is as follows: [It is as follows:]...

Hili hili hili hili, mili mili mili mili, Mālini Caṅkali, kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri, for the Brahmā Ratnakaraṇḍaka, viḍāphu viḍāphuse, dhara dhara, hara hara, hule hule, phuru phuru phuru phuru phuru svāhā.

The poison is destroyed, the poison is struck down; the poison is destroyed by the splendor of the Buddha, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of the Pratyekabuddha, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of the Arhat, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of the Anāgāmin, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of the Sakṛdāgāmin, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of the Śrotāpanna, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of truthful speech, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of Brahma’s staff, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of Indra’s thunderbolt, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of Viṣṇu’s discus, the poison is destroyed by the splendor of fire, and the poison is destroyed by the splendor of Varuṇa’s noose.

Poison struck down by the magic of the Asuras; poison struck down by the spells of the Nāgas; poison struck down by the fiery power of Rudra’s trident; poison struck down by the fiery power of Skanda’s spear; and poison struck down by the Mahāmāyūrī spell.

May the poison pass into the earth; may there be well-being for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings, from every poison: from *vatsanābha* poison, *halāhala* poison, *kālakūṭa* poison, fang-poison, root-poison, lightning-poison, cloud-obscuration-poison, *cuṇḍa* poison, *hṛṣṭi* poison, cloud-poison, snake-poison, from the poison of *lūṭaka*, insects, spiders, frogs, flies, bees, *tryambuka*, and *trailāṭaka* creatures, from *garuḍa*-poison, and human-poison.

From the poison of non-humans, from the poison of Śakra, from the poison of medicinal herbs, and from the poison of spells—may there be well-being from all poisons! Svāhā to the monk Svāti, and to me and to all sentient beings, svāhā!
And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās, has been spoken and approved by Śakra, the lord of the gods, as follows:

Jala jantu le! Cāpeṭi jantu le! Mathani ghaṭani grasani! Hari hari śiri dyoti! Śire tataru tataru! Ṇabati siṃhā! Hā hā hā hā hā! Siṃhe dhiti dhiti kuru kuru! Śabare vajre jyoti tuṭa tuṭasi! Baṭa baṭasi! Sili sili! Kapile! Kapilamūle hā hī hūm! I perform the crushing of all the wicked and the extremely wicked. I perform the restraint of their hands, feet, and limbs.
"Vajra, vajra, vajra, vajra, vajra, vajra, to the Lord of Vajras, together with the thirty-three gods, O wielder of the thunderbolt, who dwells with the Lord of the Gods, svāhā!
And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Spells, has been spoken and approved by the four Great Kings, as follows:"

Blaze, O burner! Heat, O heater! Burn, O inflamer! Protect, O refuge! Strike with the brow, strike with the brow! Strike with the fist, strike with the fist! Pierce, pierce! Kill, kill! Seize, seize! Support, support! Titi tiri! Ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa! Dā dā dā dā dā! Vā vā vā vā vā! Hale hale hale hale hale! Siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi! Svasti svasti svasti svasti svasti! For me and for all sentient beings, svāhā! (Mmk Taku 47)

May there be well-being from all messengers; from Kālarātri; from the noose of Time; from the staff of Death; from the staff of Brahmā; from the staff of Indra; from the staff of the Ṛṣis; from the staff of the gods; from the staff of the Nāgas; from the staff of the Asuras; from the staff of the Maruts; from the staff of Garuḍa; from the staff of the Gandharvas; from the staff of the Kinnaras; from the staff of the Mahoragas; from the staff of the Yakṣas; from the staff of the Rākṣasas; from the staff of the Pretas; from the staff of the Piśācas; from the staff of the Bhūtas; and from the staff of the Kumbhāṇḍas.

From the rod of the *pūtana* spirits, from the rod of the *kaṭapūtana* spirits, from the rod of *skanda*, from the rod of madness, from the rod of *ostāraka* demons, from the rod of *vetāḍa* spirits, from the rod of kings, from the rod of thieves, from the rod of fire, from the rod of water—from all such rods and pits—may there be well-being! May they provide protection for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Ānanda, you should take up the names of the queens of rivers. They are as follows:

The Gaṅgā, queen of rivers; the Sindhu, queen of rivers; the Sītā, queen of rivers; the Vakṣu, queen of rivers; the Śarayū, queen of rivers; the Ajiravatī, queen of rivers; the Yamunā, queen of rivers; the Kuhā, queen of rivers; the Vitastā, queen of rivers; the Śatabāhu, queen of rivers; the Vipāśā, queen of rivers; the Airāvatī, queen of rivers; the Candrabhāgā, queen of rivers; the Sarasvatī, queen of rivers; the Kacchapī, queen of rivers; the Payoṣṇī, queen of rivers; the Kāvelī, queen of rivers; the Tāmraparṇī, queen of rivers.

The queen of rivers Madhumatī, the queen of rivers Vetravatī, the queen of rivers Ikṣumatī, the queen of rivers Puṣkiriṇī, the queen of rivers Gomatī, the queen of rivers Carmadā, the queen of rivers Narmadā, the queen of rivers Saumitrā, the queen of rivers Viśvamitrā, the queen of rivers Amarā, the queen of rivers Tāmarā, the queen of rivers Pañcālā, the queen of rivers Suvāstu, the queen of rivers Prabhadrikā, the queen of rivers Tapodā, the queen of rivers Vimalā, the queen of rivers Nairañjanā, the queen of rivers Hiraṇyavatī, and the queen of rivers Rathasyā.

These and other great rivers flow upon this terrestrial sphere. In all those rivers dwell gods, nāgas, asuras, maruts, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanās, kaṭapūtanās, skandas, unmādas, chāyās, apasmāras, ostārakas, oja-hāras, garbha-hāras, rudhira-hāras, māṃsa-hāras, vasā-hāras, meda-hāras, majjā-hāras, jāta-hāras, and jīvita-hāras.

There dwell resident beings of various forms, misshapen, with diverse appearances, and of infinite forms; they are capable of assuming any form at will and possess variegated shapes. They subsist on vomit, on strength-giving food, on garlands, on perfumes, on flowers, on incense, on grain, on oblations, on pus, on excrement, on urine, on spittle, on phlegm, on snivel, on leftovers, on impurities, and on runoff from drains.

May they also, by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells (*mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī*), provide protection, defense, rescue, guardianship, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Ānanda, take up the names of the kings of mountains, as follows:

Sumeru, king of mountains; Himavat, king of mountains; Gandhamādana, king of mountains; Śataśṛṅga, king of mountains; Khadiraka, king of mountains; Suvarṇapārśva, king of mountains; Vidyudhdhara, king of mountains; Dyutindhara, king of mountains; Nimindhara, king of mountains; Cakravāḍa, king of mountains; Mahācakravāḍa, king of mountains; Indraśaila, king of mountains; Brahmālaya, king of mountains; and the Śrīmant mountains.

Parvatarāja, Sudarśana Parvatarāja, Vipula Parvatarāja, Ratnākara Parvatarāja, Asuraprāgbhāra Parvatarāja, Kṛmila Parvatarāja, Maṇikūṭa Parvatarāja, Vemacitra Parvatarāja, Vajrākara Parvatarāja, Asuraprāgbhāra Parvatarāja, Hanucitra Parvatarāja, Vidyutprabha Parvatarāja, Aśvastha Parvatarāja, Candraprabha Parvatarāja, and Bhadraśaila.

Parvatarāja, Sūryākānta Parvatarāja, Vindu Parvatarāja, Vindhya Parvatarāja, Śaila Parvatarāja, Citrakūṭa Parvatarāja, Malaya Parvatarāja, Suvarṇaśṛṅga Parvatarāja, Parijāta Parvatarāja, Subāhu Parvatarāja, Maṇimant Parvatarāja, Suṣena Parvatarāja, Brahmadaṇḍa Parvatarāja, Vedagaccha Parvatarāja, Gokarṇa Parvatarāja, and Mālyacitra.

Parvatarāja, Khaḍga Parvatarāja, Tāpana Parvatarāja, Arjana Parvatarāja, Saṃgama Parvatarāja, Rurubha Parvatarāja, Darada Parvatarāja, Śaṅkha Parvatarāja, Modaka Parvatarāja, Candanamāla Parvatarāja, Gopagiri Parvatarāja, Kailāsa Parvatarāja, Mahendra Parvatarāja, Sahya Parvatarāja, Upātiṣṭhi Parvatarāja, and Candramāla Parvatarāja.
Mount Vallūlagṛha, Mount Kākanāda, and Mount Śāsananāda—

these and other mountain kings on this terrestrial mandala are inhabited by gods, nāgas, asuras, maruts, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanās, kaṭapūtanās, skandas, unmādas, chāyās, apasmāras, ostārakas, siddhas, vidyādharas, and kings with their retinues, who dwell there as permanent residents.

May they also, by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells, provide protection, defense, rescue, guardianship, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings; may they live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns. May they remove all evils, may they behold only what is auspicious and cause the inauspicious to perish;
may they behold only what is beneficial and ward off what is harmful.
May there be well-being for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings.
May there be well-being at night, well-being by day, and well-being when midday has arrived.
May all the Buddhas grant you well-being throughout the entire day and night.
"Take up, Ānanda, the names of the constellations that move through the sky and illuminate it. They are as follows:
Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya—which is endowed with auspiciousness—and Aśleṣā is the seventh."

Thus, these seven constellations situated at the eastern gate—those which guard and protect the eastern direction—by means of this *Mahāmāyūrī*, the Queen of Vidyās, may they provide protection for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings. May they grant us defense, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May [the donor] live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. It is as follows:
Maghā, Arthanī (Pūrvaphalgunī), both Phalgunīs, as well as Hastā, Citrā, Svātī, and Viśākhā is the seventh.

Thus, these seven constellations situated at the southern gate—those which guard and protect the southern direction—by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of vidyās, may they provide protection, defense, rescue, shelter, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may they live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Anurādhā, Mahātejā, Jeṣṭhā, and likewise Mūlā, Pūrvā-āṣāḍhā and Uttara-āṣāḍhā, as well as Abhijit and Śravaṇa—
these seven constellations are situated at the western gate; they guard and protect the western direction.

May they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī Queen of Spells, provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns.
Dhaṇiṣṭhā and Śatabhiṣā, both Bhādrapadas likewise, Revatī, Aśvinī, and Bharaṇī as the seventh.

Thus, these seven constellations situated at the northern gate—those which guard and protect the northern direction—by means of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of vidyās, may they provide protection, concealment, rescue, acceptance, preservation, peace, and well-being for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings. May they provide the avoidance of punishment, the avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May [the donor] live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

"Take up, Ānanda, and memorize the names of the planets, those planets which, moving among the constellations, announce decrease and increase, happiness and suffering, security, and both abundance and famine.
They are as follows: the planet Sūrya, the planet Candra, the planet Bṛhaspati, the planet Śukra, the planet Śanaiścara, the planet Aṅgāra, and the planet Budha."
Rāhu, the lord of the Asuras, is a planet; Dhūmaketu is a planet;
there are twenty-eight lunar mansions situated seven in each direction.
Likewise, there are five star-planets, with Rāhu and Ketu as the seventh.
Possessing great splendor, great strength, great supernatural power,
and great asceticism, they are no fewer than thirty-seven, including the sun and the moon;
they occupy the positions of rising and setting, and have the wheel, the transition, and weapons as their arms.

May those of great splendor and great supernatural power, who cause the decline and increase [of merit] in the world, rejoice in this vidyā with a most serene mind. May they, by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Vidyās, provide protection for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings; may they grant security, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, the avoidance of punishment, the avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

"Ānanda, take up the names of the ancient great seers—those perfected ones who have accomplished their vows, accomplished their sciences, whose ascetic heat is blazing, who dwell by rivers and mountains, who have curses as their weapons, who possess fierce splendor, who are endowed with supernatural power, who possess the five superknowledges, and who travel through the air. I shall proclaim their names. They are as follows:"

The great seer named Aṣṭamaka; the great seer named Vāmadevaka; the great seer named Vāmaka; the great seer named Mārīci; the great seer named Mārkaṇḍeya; the great seer named Viśvāmitra; the great seer named Vasiṣṭha; the great seer named Kāśyapa; the great seer named Balamīka; the great seer named Vṛddhakāśyapa; the great seer named Bhṛgu; the great seer named Bhṛṅgirasa; the great seer named Aṅgirasa; the great seer named Bhṛṅgī; and Baṭṭa.

the great seer named Nāma, the great seer named Bhāgiratha, the great seer named Aṅgīrasa, the great seer named Ātreya, the great seer named Paurastya, the great seer named Sthūlaśiras, the great seer named Yamadagni, the great seer named Dvaipsāyana, the great seer named Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, the great seer named Harita, the great seer named Haritāyana, the great seer named Samaṅgira, the great seer named Udgata, and the great seer named Samudgata.

The great seer named Kṣāntivādī; the great seer named Kīrti; the great seer named Sukīrti; the great seer named Guru; the great seer named Śarabha; the great seer named Mardana; the great seer named Potalaka; the great seer named Aśvalāyana; the great seer named Himavat; the great seer named Lohitākṣa; the great seer named Durvāsas; the great seer named Vaiśampāyana; the great seer named Vālmīki; the great seer named Surata; and the one named Madana.

The great seer named Manu, the great seer named Prabha, the great seer named Śukra, the great seer named Bṛhaspati, the great seer named Aranemi, the great seer named Śanaiścara, the great seer named Budha, the great seer named Jāṅgulī, the great seer named Gandhāra, the great seer named Ekaśṛṅga, the great seer named Ṛṣiśṛṅga, the great seer named Garga, the great seer named Gārgyāyana, and the one named Bhāṇḍāyana.

The great seer named Kātyāyana; the great seer named Kāṇḍyāyana; the great seer named Bhīṣma; the great seer named Bhīṣmamātaṅga; the great seer named Kapila; the great seer named Gautama; the great seer named Mātaṅga; the great seer named Lohitāśva; the great seer named Sunetra; the great seer named Suranemi; the great seer named Asita; the great seer named Bālikhilya; the great seer named Nārada; the great seer named Parvata; and the great seer named Kṛmila.

Thus, Ānanda, these are the ancient great seers, the authors of the Vedas, the promulgators of the mantras, the givers of curses, possessed of fierce power and great splendor, and perfected in their prowess.

May they also, by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells, provide protection, defense, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns. That is to say: tadyathā.

Hiri hiri hiri, khiri khiri, miri miri, muri muri, hiri hiri, mili mili, ḍaphu ḍaphu ḍaphu, mathani, ghāṭani, pacani pācani, dahani dāhani, tapani tāpani, hanani, daha daha dahani, tālani pātani mojani sta stani jastani svayaṃbhūve svāhā.

"Ānanda, you should memorize the names of Mahāprajāpatī, and those of the gods, nāgas, maruts, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, humans, non-humans, animals, celestial beings, hell-beings, and others—both auspicious and inauspicious—who, through countless varieties of blessings, are established throughout the three worlds. They are as follows:"

Brahmā Prajāpati, Atri Prajāpati, Ātreya Prajāpati, Agni Prajāpati, Bhṛgu Prajāpati, Pulastya Prajāpati, Pulaha Prajāpati, Manu Prajāpati, Vasiṣṭha Prajāpati, Duṣṭa Prajāpati, Sutanu Prajāpati, Sunandamāna Prajāpati, Dakṣa Prajāpati, and Sanatkumāra Prajāpati.

Thus, Ānanda, these great-souled Prajāpatis are established for the sake of protecting the multitude of beings, both stationary and moving; may they also, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās, provide protection, guard, rescue, support, preservation, peace, and well-being for me, the monk Svāti, and for all sentient beings; may they provide the warding off of punishment, the warding off of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; may he live!
May he see a hundred autumns, a hundred years. By these unassailable mantra-words, may protection be granted for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. Namely:

*hiri hiri, khiri khiri, mili mili, sili sili, hili hili, mili mili sili sili, ḍaphu ḍaphu ḍaḍaphu, grasani mathani dahani ghātani, pacani pācani, hanani dāhani, dala dala dālani pāṭani mohani sta stanī jambhanīye svāhā*. Take up, Ānanda, the names of the great poisons. Namely:

Aṇḍarā, Paṇḍarā, Karaḍā, Keyūrā, Bhūtāṅgamā, Bhūtapati, Vindupati, Śiripati, Tejapati, Tejograpati, Yaśopati, Araḍā, Taraḍā, Taradā, Tarataraḍā, Duttarā, Dantājuhā, Juhā, Johā, Jolā, Melā, Phurā, Guhā, Rucirā, Danturā, Ilīkicikā, Kirikirikā, Kāmvā, Śatanturā, Vikuli, Kirimi, Taraṅgā, Riṣṭā, Āmravatī, Jambumatī, Manumatī, Kamale, Vimale, Kuṇḍale.
To Ahituṇḍika, to Duhitṛ, to Vakva, to Vakvadūta, to Vatsamātṛ, to Mahāgāra, to Tulamva, to Sulamva, svāhā!

"Ānanda, may these great poisons—by means of this Great Peacock Queen of Spells—provide protection, guarding, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralizing of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings. May they live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Ānanda, take up the names of the great trees. They are as follows:"

There was a great tree named Kāñcana, a great tree named Pippala, a great tree named Aśvatthāna, a great tree named Kapitthāna, a great tree named Udumbara, a great tree named Kapītuka, a great tree named Śāla, a great tree named Karṇikāra, a great tree named Tiniśa, a great tree named Bilva, a great tree named Cūta, and a great tree named Nicūta.

These and other great trees, and the deities who dwell within them—may they, by means of this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās, provide protection for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings; may they grant guard, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; may he live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.

And this, Ānanda, Mahāmāyūrī, the queen of vidyās, has been spoken of and rejoiced in by seven perfectly awakened ones. Namely: it was spoken of and rejoiced in by the perfectly awakened Vipaśyin; it was spoken of and rejoiced in by the perfectly awakened Śikhin; it was spoken of and rejoiced in by the perfectly awakened Viśvabhū; it was spoken of and rejoiced in by the perfectly awakened Krakucchanda; [and it was spoken of and rejoiced in] by Kanakamuni...

It was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One; it was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened Kāśyapa; and now it has been spoken and approved by me, Śākyamuni, the Perfectly Awakened One. Furthermore, Ānanda, this Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells was spoken and approved by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, and it was spoken and approved by Brahmā Sahāmpati.

It was spoken and approved by Śakra, the lord of the gods, and by the four Great Kings: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, king of the gandharvas; Virūḍhaka, king of the kumbhāṇḍas; Virūpākṣa, king of the nāgas; and Vaiśravaṇa, king of the yakṣas.

It was also spoken of and rejoiced in by twenty-eight generals of the gandharvas, twenty-eight generals of the kumbhāṇḍas, twenty-eight generals of the nāgas, twenty-eight generals of the yakṣas, and by the yakṣa general Pāñcika, as well as by Hārītī with her retinue of five hundred sons.

And this, Ānanda, Queen of Spells Mahāmāyūrī, is not to be transgressed by the seizure of a god, a nāga, an asura, a marut, a garuḍa, a gandharva, a kinnara, a mahoraga, a yakṣa, a rākṣasa, a preta, a piśāca, a bhūta, a kumbhāṇḍa, a pūtana, a kaṭapūtana, a skanda, an unmāda, a chāyā, or an apasmāra.

By means of the *ostāraka* [seizing] grasp. It is not to be transgressed by any planets (*graha*), nor is it to be transgressed by any of those who carry away [beings], such as: she who carries away the fetus, she who carries away the fat, she who carries away the flesh, she who carries away the marrow, she who carries away the life-force, she who carries away the strength, she who carries away the garlands, she who carries away the blood, she who carries away those already born, she who carries away perfumes, she who carries away flowers, she who carries away incense, she who carries away fruits, she who carries away crops, she who carries away the sacrificial oblation (*āhuti*), she who carries away pus, she who carries away excrement, she who carries away urine, and she who carries away saliva.

[She is] one who eats phlegm, one who eats snoring, one who eats leftovers, one who eats vomit, one who eats excrement, one who eats impurity, and one who eats nasal mucus. She is not to be transgressed by means of malevolent rites (*kṛtyā*), magical operations (*karmaṇa*), spells (*kākhorda*), scattering [of powders], raising of corpses (*vetāḍa*), the dispatching of *cicca* spirits, ill-eaten food, ill-vomited food, bad shadows, ill-gazed-at sights, ill-drawn figures, or being stepped over, nor by those who have shaken off [the protection].

It is not to be transgressed by fever—whether it be quotidian, tertian, quartan, weekly, half-monthly, monthly, bi-monthly, momentary, constant, or irregular; whether caused by spirits, by humans, or by non-humans; whether arising from wind, bile, phlegm, or a combination of all three. It is not to be transgressed by any fevers whatsoever.

It is not to be transgressed by headache, by hemicrania, by loss of appetite, by eye disease, by nose disease, by mouth disease, by throat disease, by ear disease, by heart disease, by lockjaw, by earache, by toothache, by heart pain, by side pain, by back pain, by abdominal pain, by cheek pain, by bladder pain, by vaginal pain, by labor pains, by calf pain, by thigh pain, by hand pain, by foot pain, or by pain in the limbs and minor members.

It is not to be transgressed by ringworm, itching, scabies, leprosy, fistula-in-ano, goiters, pustules, scabies, erysipelas, or jaundice. It is not to be transgressed by any diseases, any malevolent influences, any poisons, or any fears. It is not to be transgressed by any strife, quarrels, conflicts, calamities, misfortunes, or distresses.

Ānanda, whoever should transgress against this Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī, Vajrapāṇi shall split his head into seven pieces like the cluster of blossoms on an arjaka tree. His vision will be destroyed by the splendor of all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas; his mind will be destroyed. He will have deceived the Noble Ones (āryapudgala), and the Four Great Kings will bring him to great ruin with weapons as sharp as razors.

Even Śakra, the lord of the gods, surrounded by the hosts of the Thirty-three, might shatter his head with the thunderbolt; and by the power of his Brahmanic splendor, his prosperity would be reduced to ashes.

But, Ānanda, for one who is protected by this Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī and to whom the thread and the *pratisarā* amulet are bound, he is released from whatever punishment he deserves: he who deserves a staff is released from the staff; he who deserves blows is released from blows; he who deserves abuse is released from abuse; he who deserves reproach is released from reproach; he who deserves to have his hair stand on end is released from that very thing. Thus indeed is he released.

Furthermore, he shall have no fear of kings, no fear of thieves, and no fear of fire; he shall not die by water, nor shall poison enter his body, nor shall a weapon strike him. He shall live long and happily; except for his former dreams, Ānanda, he shall awaken in peace—secure, free from affliction, undaunted, with adversaries and enemies subdued, and unharmed.
Completely freed from all fear of poison, he will live happily for a long time, Ānanda, except for the ripening of his past karma.

And this, Ānanda, the Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells, should be recited during excessive rain or in a drought. Thereupon, all the nāgas will become eager, thinking, "She will restrain the excessive rain," and in the case of a drought, "She will cause a downpour of rain. As long as the intention of that son of good family or daughter of good family persists, for so long will the god send rain. And, Ānanda, by the mere recollection of this Mahāmāyūrī queen of spells, all fears and enmities will be pacified.
How much more so, then, for one who would uphold, recite, or perform the rite of well-being for this entire, complete, and unbroken [text]!

Ānanda, you must take up this Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī; master it, uphold it, and recite this Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī, which pacifies all fears and enmities, for the sake of the protection, defense, and guardianship of my fourfold assembly—of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen. It is as follows:
*yāvati dhāvati balaki kuru tulu me svāhā*. Protect me and all sentient beings, svāhā!
Passion, hatred, and delusion—these are the three poisons in the world.
The Blessed Buddha is free from poison; the poison is destroyed by the truth of the Buddha.
Passion, hatred, and delusion—these are the three poisons in the world.
The Dharma of the Blessed One is free from poison; poison is destroyed by the truth of the Dharma.
Lust, hatred, and delusion—these three are the poisons in the world;
the Saṅgha of the Blessed One is free from poison; poison is destroyed by the truth of the Saṅgha.
If it is sufficient for the glory of all the Buddhas and Arhats, then by the splendor of the Tathāgata, this auspicious rite has been performed by me.
"The poison has been destroyed for the monk Svāti, for me, and for all sentient beings;

may the Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Spells, belong to the monk Svāti and to me. "Excellent, Blessed One! the venerable Ānanda replied. Having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and circumambulated the Blessed One three times, he approached the monk Svāti and performed a protection for the monk Svāti with this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Spells.

He performed protection, rescue, shelter, preservation, peace, auspiciousness, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; and the venerable monk Svāti recovered from that illness once the venerable Ānanda had provided this protection and auspicious rite.

Then the venerable Ānanda and the monk Svāti approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and reported everything exactly as it had occurred. Being permitted by the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.

Then the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda, "Have you seen the power of the Great Peacock Queen of Spells? Ānanda, having prostrated to the Blessed One who had spoken thus, replied, "How could this not be known, Blessed One? The Blessed One spoke again:

"Even if, Ānanda, the four great oceans were to dry up, or the earth were to arise as space, or the moon and sun were to fall to the earth, or rivers were to flow upstream, the word of the Tathāgata would not be otherwise. Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda.

"Therefore, Ānanda, you should proclaim this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās, for the protection, shelter, and guardianship of the fourfold assembly—of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen. "Very well, Blessed One," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and having so agreed, he proclaimed this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās, to the fourfold assembly: to the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.

Thus spoke the Blessed One. The Venerable Ānanda, the Venerable Svāti, and the monks who were assembled and seated in that assembly—along with the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, humans, and non-humans—all rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said. This concludes the *Bhagavatī Āryamahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī*, the nine-hundred-verse [text] spoken by the Buddha, recovered unimpaired from the mouth of a yakṣa.
"Protect me and all sentient beings; may there be well-being and prosperity.

This is the ritual procedure for this Mahāmāyūrī, the Queen of Vidyās: On a clean spot of ground, having smeared a sacrificial altar (*sthaṇḍila*) the size of a cow-hide with fresh, tawny cow-dung, one should fashion a square mandala using whatever cow-dung is available for the purpose at hand.

And there, in the center, an image of the Buddha should be placed facing west; on its left side, a manuscript of the Mahāmāyūrī should be placed, either written out or made as a painted work, or else three peacock eyes (mayūracandrikā) should be placed sitting upon cow dung that is tawny-brown. Then, having offered white Arka flowers, white Karavīra and Bilva leaves, and Śirīṣa leaves, one should offer the bali-oblation consisting of sesame, rice-pudding, sesame-water, and milk-rice.

Having offered vessels filled with molasses, barley-gruel, honey, and cooked rice according to what is available, and having offered guggulu incense while facing east, one should then face south, west, and north, making offerings to the four quarters for the yakṣas of the four directions mentioned previously, and say: "Come! Accept these flowers, incense, perfumes, offerings, and lamps; protect me and all sentient beings. *Oṃ varade hūṃ hariṇi sphuṭ kāriṇi svāhā.*

In that regard, milk-rice filled with jaggery should be placed in the eastern direction; that is the offering for the Gandharvas. A vessel filled with sesame, rice-gruel, and liquor should be placed in the southern direction; that is the offering for the Kumbhāṇḍas. Milk-rice filled with milk should be placed in the western direction; that is the offering for the Nāgas and Suparṇīs. Curd-rice filled with river-water should be placed in the northern direction; that is the offering for the Yakṣas. Thus ends the Great Queen of Spells named Ārya-Mahāmāyūrī.
Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has declared their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
